title: Software Composition Analysis
summary: Software composition analysis is the automated identification of third-party and open-source components in a codebase or built artifact, together with an assessment of the known vulnerabilities, licence obligations and maintenance risks attached to those components. A typical SCA engine resolves the dependency graph from manifests and lock files, matches resolved versions against vulnerability advisories, and reports the direct and transitive path that introduces each affected package, which matters because most findings arrive through dependencies the team never chose explicitly. Modern supply-chain expectations extend SCA to artifact-level analysis of containers and binaries, where the tool inspects package databases inside an image rather than trusting the build manifest alone. For a practising engineer the hard parts are reachability, version-range ambiguity and remediation logistics. A flagged transitive dependency may never be loaded at runtime, an advisory may apply only to a configuration the project does not use, and the fixed version may be blocked by an incompatible major upgrade somewhere else in the graph. A workable programme therefore gates on new critical findings with an available fix, tracks unfixable findings as accepted risk with an expiry, and uses override or exclusion mechanisms deliberately rather than pinning stale versions forever. The recurring failure modes are reporting the same vulnerable library dozens of times because it appears in several images, ignoring transitive dependencies entirely, and treating an empty scan result on a project that vendors its dependencies as evidence of safety.
objectives: You will be able to explain how a dependency graph is resolved from manifests and lock files and why lock files determine what is actually built.
You will be able to interpret a transitive dependency finding and trace the path that introduces the affected package.
You will be able to assess whether a vulnerable component is reachable and whether the advisory applies to the way the project uses it.
You will be able to define a gating policy that blocks new critical findings with available fixes without freezing the dependency graph.
You will be able to explain how container and binary artifact scanning differs from manifest-based analysis and when each is required.
You will be able to record accepted dependency risk with an owner, a compensating control and a review date.

beginner.definition: Software composition analysis finds the third-party and open-source parts inside your project. It reads your dependency files, matches versions against known vulnerability lists, and reports which packages are affected. It also shows the path that pulled each risky package in, so you know who to ask for a fix.
beginner.whyItMatters: Most of your application is code you did not write. That code can carry known security holes for years. Attackers watch these public lists and target anyone who is slow to update. Composition analysis turns a huge dependency tree into a short list of things to fix. Without it, you are trusting hundreds of strangers blindly.
howItWorks: The tool reads your manifest and lock files to learn every dependency.
A lock file records the exact versions that were really installed.
It builds a tree showing which package brought in each other package.
It compares those exact versions against public databases that list known vulnerabilities.
You get a report naming the package, the flaw, and the upgrade that fixes it.
You then decide to patch, replace, or formally accept the risk.
beginner.example: Think of a car made from parts produced by fifty different factories. One factory announces a brake part that can fail. A good mechanic can look up your car's parts list and tell you within minutes if your model is affected. Composition analysis is that lookup for software. It saves you from recalling every car ever made just to find the few with the bad part.
takeaways: Composition analysis finds risky third-party libraries and shows where they came from.
Indirect dependencies matter most, because you never chose them.
Block new critical findings that have a fix available today.
